title: A beautiful example
hookLine: in the messenger of Allah you have a beautiful example (33:21)
carry: do the hard thing with them

lines: DIGGING A TRENCH IN THE COLD.
cards: Medina, under threat. A confederacy of tribes is marching on the city. On the advice of Salman the Persian, the biographies say, the Muslims decide to dig a trench across the open side of the city.
Men with picks and baskets, in the cold, short on food, racing against time. And among them, carrying earth on his back until the dust covered his skin, the leader of the community.
Surah Al-Ahzab, the Confederates, the thirty-third, tells of those days.

teach.b: The surah describes the fear honestly. Eyes grew wild, hearts reached the throats, and people began to think all kinds of thoughts about God. Some slipped away with excuses.

And right in the middle of that account comes the verse. Pickthall: "Verily in the messenger of Allah ye have a good example for him who looketh unto Allah and the Last Day, and remembereth Allah much."
The Arabic is uswatun hasanah. Hasanah is good, beautiful, excellent. Uswah is a model, someone you copy.
The verse isn't on a poster. It's in a trench.
Bukhari reports that the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ dug and carried earth alongside everyone, chanting verses with them as they worked.
Jabir reported that when a huge rock blocked the digging, the Prophet came and broke it, and that he had a stone tied against his stomach from hunger, the same as the rest.
The example wasn't in how he talked about hardship. It was in doing the hardship with them.

That's what Muslims mean by following the sunnah, the Prophet's way: not only the prayers and fasts, but small things. Smiling, which a hadith calls charity. Helping at home, which 'A'isha said he did, serving his family.
Greeting first. Eating with the right hand. The Qur'an uses uswah of Ibrahim, too.
This week's lines, from Luqman to As-Sajdah, ran from Luqman's first advice and a mother's wahn, through a lowered voice and words that don't run out, to up in the night and joy kept hidden.

how: Muslims follow the sunnah, the Prophet's example, in worship and in daily habits, learning it from the hadith collections and from biographies of his life.

o: a model to copy, someone whose way you follow
a trench dug to protect a besieged city
a promise of victory after hard times

games.q: a beautiful example — tap the pairs.
p: a model, a pattern to copy
a stone tied to his stomach
hunger, the same as the rest
he helped and served at home

s: 33:21 was revealed in a calm time of peace
it sits in the account of the Trench, under siege, in fear.
the Prophet dug and carried earth with the companions
Bukhari reports him carrying earth and chanting with them.
the sunnah means only prayer and fasting
it includes small habits too: smiling, helping at home, greeting first.

games.q: you lead a frightened city under siege. a trench must be dug in the cold, on little food. what do you do?
o: direct the work from a safe distance.
dig and carry earth alongside everyone.
wait for the enemy at the walls.
games.why: Bukhari reports that the Prophet dug and carried earth with them, hungry like the rest; 33:21 calls him a beautiful example.

practice: Choose one small, everyday thing the Prophet is reported to have done: smiling at the next person you meet, helping with a chore unasked, saying salam first, sitting down to drink, eating with the right hand and saying bismillah.
Pick just one, and picture the moment in your day where it fits. If you're not Muslim, you can still pick one as a kindness worth trying.

wordCard.voice: Uswah. A model to copy; uswatun hasanah, the beautiful example the Qur'an names in the Prophet, in the middle of the trench. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a beautiful example; uswah is a model to copy, hasanah is good or beautiful.

carryVoice: Your line: do the hard thing with them. An example is shown, not told. That closes the week.
